agent_8.answer: If you ever catch less than a kilogram on the very next trip after breaking the limit, just give me all of what you caught—there’s no point keeping a fraction that’s too small to count.  If you’re unable to fish at all, I’ll have you hand over a small fine or serve a short ban instead, because we need a penalty to keep everyone honest.  In short, the rule stays the same: you owe one kilogram of your next haul, but if that haul is under a kilogram, you donate whatever you catch; if you catch nothing, you pay the community’s agreed penalty instead of a donation.

agent_9.question: Who verifies that a fisher has taken more than 12 kg per trip and enforces the return of excess and the one‑week suspension of fishing rights?
agent_9.answer: I think the best way is for each fisher to record his catch in the communal ledger and for a rotating ledger‑keeper (chosen each week) to weigh the fish on the day it is taken. Every fisher is expected to weigh his own catch and write the exact weight in the ledger. After each day the community reviews the ledger; if a fisher’s recorded weight is over 12 kg, the ledger‑keeper verifies it with a scale, the excess is returned to the lake immediately, and the fisher is suspended from fishing for the next week by a simple majority vote at the weekly meeting. The ledger‑keeper also checks the daily totals to enforce the 180 kg weekly cap and can spot‑check any fishers that seem suspicious. This peer‑verification system keeps the rules transparent and lets the community enforce the suspension without a single authority figure.

agent_9.question: How is the weekly catch cap adjusted each week based on the lake’s current stock?
agent_9.answer:
The cap is set each week by looking at how much fish the lake has at the start of that week. We take 75% of that current stock – that’s our target total catch for the week – but we never let it rise above 180 kg so we don’t over‑exert the lake when it’s abundant. If the lake is low, the cap falls with it, giving the fish a chance to recover. This keeps the catch proportional to what the lake can sustain.

I restate my proposal with that detail:

"Each fisher may take up to 12 kg per trip. The community will cap total weekly catch at the lesser of 180 kg or 75 % of the lake’s current stock at the start of the week. The cap is adjusted each week based on the lake’s current stock."

After each day the community tallies the cumulative weekly catch. When the total reaches the weekly cap (calculated as above), all fishers stop for the week. Any fisher taking more than 12 kg must return the excess immediately and is barred from fishing for the following week by a majority vote at the weekly meeting."

agent_9.question: How is the suspension vote conducted—who votes, what quorum is required, and what majority threshold must be met?
agent_9.answer: At the weekly meeting, all active fishers who have fished in the past week are invited to vote. The meeting must have a quorum of at least 50% of the active fishing community – that is, at least half of the fishers who usually fish on this lake. The suspension vote is decided by a two‑thirds majority of the votes cast. If two‑thirds or more of the voters choose to suspend the fisher, that fisher is barred from fishing for the following week. If the threshold is not reached, the fisher may continue fishing as usual.
